samples.summary: The new `resolvePageSetup` clamp is bypassed by the PDF and DOCX exporters, which read `doc.pageSetup` raw — so the unusable geometry the clamp exists to neutralise still reaches them
samples.evidence: `resolvePageSetup`'s new docstring (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:796-802) asserts it is "the single read path — the editor, the ruler, `MemDocStore`, `YorkieDocStore`, the CLI's pagination and PDF export all reach the page setup through it". That is false for the exporters: `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:87` does `const setup = doc.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP;` and then `getEffectiveDimensions(setup)` / `paginateLayout(layout, setup)` at :88-92, and `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:162` does `buildSectPrXml(doc.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP, ...)`. Neither calls `resolvePageSetup`. The value they read is exactly the unvalidated one the clamp was added for: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:530-543` (`readPageSetup`) builds `document.pageSetup` with `Number(ps?.width)` / `Number(m?.top)`, which is `NaN` for a missing or non-numeric CRDT field, and `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-export-button.tsx:53` hands precisely `editor.getStore().getDocument()` to the PDF/DOCX exporters. Result: a partially-written or hostile `root.pageSetup` yields NaN page width/height and NaN margins in the exported PDF (NaN `x`/`y`/page sizes) and `w:w="NaN"` in the exported .docx — a corrupt file, produced silently.

samples.summary: `formatSourcePosition()`'s unconditional `+1` reads the wrong run when the selection starts at the very end of a block, or for an unordered table-cell-rectangle range
samples.evidence: `formatSourcePosition` returns `{ blockId: normalized.start.blockId, offset: normalized.start.offset + 1 }`. Two cases give the run that is *not* the first selected character: (a) a multi-block selection whose start offset equals the start block's text length — the first selected character actually lives in the *next* block, but `caretInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/model/caret-style.ts:64) falls back to the start block's *last* run, i.e. the run immediately before the selection, which is the exact defect the `+1` was introduced to fix; (b) for a `tableCellRange`, `normalizeRange` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:120-128) returns `start: range.anchor` **without ordering**, so a backward cell drag copies the format at the anchor, plus one character, rather than the range's start.

samples.summary: `HAS_SCHEME` misclassifies a relative reference containing a colon as absolute, silently dropping a legitimate link/image target
samples.evidence: `isEmittableUrl` routes anything matching `/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:/` through `isSafeUrl`. A relative path whose first segment contains a colon — e.g. `notes:2024.md`, `a.png:80`, or a Windows-style `C:/x` — matches that pattern, so `new URL()` reads it as protocol `notes:` / `a.png:` / `c:`, none of which is on the allowlist, and the reference is dropped: the href degrades to bare text and the image to `[image]`. The comment at :286-293 states relative references are accepted precisely so legitimate content is not stripped; this class of them is not.

samples.summary: `assertUsablePageSetup` throws `TypeError`, not `RangeError`, when the caller passes a setup with a missing `paperSize` or `margins`
samples.evidence: `assertUsablePageSetup(setup)` immediately calls `getEffectiveDimensions(setup)`, which dereferences `setup.paperSize.width` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:844), and then reads `setup.margins[side]`. `EditorAPI.setPageSetup` is public and reachable from untyped JS/CLI callers; a `{}` or `{ paperSize: undefined }` produces an uncaught `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` from inside the editor rather than the documented `RangeError`, and the error message template at :2970 (`${setup.paperSize.width}×...`) would throw again while being built.

samples.summary: `setPageSetup` can silently store margins different from the ones the caller passed, contradicting its own "throws rather than clamping" rationale
samples.evidence: `assertUsablePageSetup` only requires `left + right < width` (content > 0), but `writePageSetup` then stores `resolvePageSetup(setup)`, whose `fitMargins` enforces a 1 px floor (`MIN_CONTENT_PX`, packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:756,783). A setup leaving e.g. 0.5 px of content passes the assert and is then proportionally rescaled on the way into the store, so a subsequent `getPageSetup()` does not return what was written — exactly the "silently substituting a different page size than the caller asked for" the comment at :959-961 says is avoided.

samples.summary: Folding line separators to a space collapses legitimate DOCX `<w:br/>` soft breaks inside a run
samples.evidence: `escapeMarkdownText` now applies `LINE_SEPARATORS -> ' '`. The DOCX importer stores a `<w:br/>` as a literal `\n` inside the run's text (packages/docs/src/import/docx-parser.ts:267-268), so an imported paragraph containing an intentional line break exports as a space rather than a break. Rendering is usually equivalent for a single soft break, but two consecutive breaks that previously produced a paragraph split now become two spaces.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: pdf-exporter.ts:87 reads `doc.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` and feeds it to getEffectiveDimensions (:88), margin arithmetic (:89) and paginateLayout (:92); a full grep of that file shows no resolvePageSetup call. docx-exporter.ts:162 does the same and buildSectPrXml (:364-373) writes the raw numbers into w:pgSz/w:pgMar via pxToTwips with no validation. The new clamp's docstring (types.ts:796-802) explicitly claims PDF export reaches page setup through resolvePageSetup and names the collaborator CRDT write as the case it guards. The unvalidated value does reach the exporters: yorkie-doc-store.ts:530-543 readPageSetup yields Number(undefined)=NaN, getDocument() at :604-606 assigns it with no clamp (while getPageSetup() at :661-666 does clamp — the two read paths disagree), and docs-export-button.tsx:53 passes getStore().getDocument() (store = YorkieDocStore, docs-view.tsx:324; editor.ts:2846 returns it unwrapped) to pdf-actions.ts:30 / docx-actions.ts:50, which forward the doc untouched. The CLI export path (commands/docs.ts:271-317) likewise passes fetchedDoc raw; only the page-count helper cli/src/docs/paginate.ts:26 resolves. I found no clamp at any hop, so no counterexample. Impact: NaN page geometry silently produces a corrupt PDF/.docx.
